Baby Corn Gratin

Served at: Feast of the Holy Innocents (Childermas Banquet)

Serves 6Prep 15 minCook 30 min

Baby Corn Gratin is a creamy, cheesy baked vegetable dish traditionally served at the Feast of the Holy Innocents, also known as Childermas Banquet. This dish symbolizes innocence and purity, fitting for a celebration honoring the children. It combines tender baby corn with a rich béchamel sauce and a golden crust, making it a comforting and festive addition to the holiday table.

Ingredients

  • 2 tablespoons unsalted butter (30 g)
  • 2 tablespoons all-purpose flour (16 g)
  • 1 1/2 cups whole milk (360 ml), warmed
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt
  • 1/4 teaspoon white pepper
  • 1/4 teaspoon ground nutmeg
  • 2 cups baby corn, fresh or thawed if frozen (300 g)
  • 1 cup grated Gruyère cheese (100 g)
  • 1/2 cup grated Parmesan cheese (50 g)
  • 1/2 cup panko breadcrumbs (50 g)
  • 1 tablespoon olive oil
  • Fresh parsley, chopped, for garnish (optional)

Method

  1. Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
  2. In a medium saucepan, melt butter over medium heat.
  3. Whisk in flour and cook for 1-2 minutes until it forms a smooth paste but does not brown.
  4. Gradually whisk in the warmed milk, continuing to stir until the sauce thickens and is smooth, about 5 minutes.
  5. Season the béchamel sauce with salt, white pepper, and nutmeg.
  6. Add the baby corn to the sauce and stir to coat evenly.
  7. Transfer the mixture to a greased baking dish (about 8x8 inches or 20x20 cm).
  8. In a small bowl, combine the Gruyère, half of the Parmesan, and panko breadcrumbs.
  9. Sprinkle the cheese and breadcrumb mixture evenly over the baby corn.
  10. Drizzle the olive oil over the topping to help it brown.
  11. Bake in the preheated oven for 25-30 minutes, until the top is golden and bubbly.
  12. Remove from oven and sprinkle with the remaining Parmesan cheese and chopped parsley if desired.
  13. Serve warm as a side dish during the Feast of the Holy Innocents.

Tips

  • For a richer flavor, substitute half the milk with cream.
  • Add finely chopped shallots or garlic to the béchamel for extra depth.
  • Use fresh baby corn when in season for the best texture and sweetness.
